page.text:
A *field* is a non-trivial commutative ring in which every nonzero
element has a multiplicative inverse: the set of nonzero elements
$F^\times = F \setminus \{0\}$ forms an abelian group under
multiplication.

Fields represent the optimal arithmetic environment: addition,
subtraction, multiplication, and division (by nonzero elements) are
universally permitted and obey all classical algebraic symmetries. Fields
provide the scalar domain for linear algebra and vector spaces, and their
algebraic extensions are the focus of Galois theory.
